bull.b: Demand is growing across several ophthalmic franchises rather than relying on one product. Rising prescriptions, ordering accounts, and surgical adoption support broader commercial traction and create a more durable revenue base as the portfolio and sales infrastructure scale.

bull.t: High margins and improving cash generation
bull.b: Very high gross margins indicate attractive product economics, while the shift to positive operating and free cash flow improves liquidity and internal funding capacity. If sustained, this combination can support commercial investment and gradually reduce reliance on external capital.

Adding TYRVAYA broadens Harrow’s dry-eye offering and may increase the value of its existing commercial platform. Expanded PBM access also enlarges the addressable patient base, supporting prescription growth and strengthening the company’s ophthalmic market position.

bear.t: Elevated leverage and thin equity cushion
bear.b: Higher leverage reduces financial flexibility and leaves less room to absorb weaker operating performance or fund expansion internally. The thin equity cushion increases sensitivity to refinancing needs and could make future capital raising more dilutive if cash generation falls short.

bear.t: Persistent losses and elevated operating costs
bear.b: Strong gross margins have not yet translated into consistent profitability, indicating that operating costs and other charges remain substantial. Continued losses can consume financial resources and make the company more dependent on successful revenue scaling and disciplined expense management.

bear.t: Execution risk from required growth ramp
bear.b: Meeting the annual outlook requires a sharp second-half acceleration across product growth, channel normalization, salesforce productivity, and TYRVAYA integration. Failure to deliver that ramp would pressure profitability, cash planning, and confidence in the company’s expansion strategy.
